comment: Gave our final group project a mark that was in no way related to the rubric or instructions. Made no effort to correct in emails even insulting our group and comparing us to middle schoolers. Very unprofessional.
Amazing and caring professor, take his class with no doubt.

The material for 222 is pretty difficult and there's a lot of confusing concepts. On top of that Dr. Gao's main language isnt English so his lectures aren't always clear. That being said you will never meet a professor who cares more about his students than him. Although there's a lot of homework and tests are hard he constantly gives extra credit

He is the best professor here at UR. He's a kind and caring guy, always willing to help students, and also a generous grader. He also provided extra credits. Sometimes you may don't understand his explanation but that's just because English is not his mother language. Be lenient! The course isn't that easy but he will help you easily go through it.

He didn't go too deep into discrete structures. This course was just a simple version of MATH300 plus some easy programming exercises. Don't worry about your grade. He had over 58 extra points on the overall grade.
I recommend students who are not going to major in Computer Science to take this course. And this is also a good course for students who know nothing about programming.

Dr. Gao fails at classroom engagement and interactive exercises. He struggles to answer simple questions asked by students and only teaches through reading out of the textbook. Overall the class isnt too difficult. The homework is manageable, although the tests are tricky. The hardest part is surviving the boring classes and long labs.

Dr. Gao is a genuinely nice guy and you can tell he has a great grasp of the material... unfortunately that doesn't help any of the students, half of whom stopped showing up to class because his lectures are less than helpful. Discrete math with him was a self study course, and not an easy one at that. He is a very lenient grader, however.

Gao is a very caring person. However, his lectures are not great and he typically assigns a good amount of homework. The class is still pretty easy, you could skip the lectures and just use the notes he gives you to do everything. His exams were also fairly straightforward. He really everything down great except for his teaching, which is fine.

Had him for intro and it was great. Discrete structures on the other hand was a complete mess. I felt like going to the class was a waste of my time. Prob explains why 90% of the class stopped showing up halfway through the semester. Extremely nice and lenient guy, but sadly he can't teach very well.

CMSC150 is an INTRO class. Don't expect to learn the really advanced stuff like the guy below. It was my first time doing python and I learned so much. Educational class and the professor being such an amazing guy is a plus

The class is really easy but you will not learn anything. Don't waste your time. Especially if you want to be a CS major this will screw you for future classes. Attendance is mandatory literally 15% of the grade was attendance, bonus points for attending too. Sometimes uploads solutions prior to due date. Bad communicator and horrible teacher.
super lenient, super easy-going, super nice, super caring. what more can I say. I dreaded having to take compsci, but he is the easiest and best professor.
Professor Gao cares about his students and makes sure they understand the material. He has a decent amount of assignments but they are pretty straightforward. Overall recommend taking.

Dr. Gao is a wonderful teacher! He is really helpful and is willing to help to student when a student comes with a question. He really helped me learn a lot about Computer Science and its fundamentals. He does not give too much work and his tests are easy too - if he student is able to understand what is happening in class.
